hints: Differentiate x ∝ t³ twice. What power of t is left?
worded:
1. Each differentiation lowers the power of t by one. From t³, velocity goes as t² and acceleration as t.

2. Acceleration proportional to t grows steadily with time. (A)

3. Contrast: constant acceleration would need x ∝ t² (option C belongs to that case).
conventional:
![](asset:P000142-sol-1)

$x = kt^{3} \Rightarrow v = 3kt^{2} \Rightarrow a = 6kt$, which increases linearly with time.
mistakes: x ∝ t³ is not uniformly accelerated motion; don’t use SUVAT for it.
